statements.label: supported
statements.text: A null ketch1 mutation is lethal to Arabidopsis embryos, while ketch1 knockdown plants show morphological defects resembling those of miRNA pathway mutants.
statements.evidence: Null mutation of ketch1 is embryonic-lethal, whereas knockdown mutation of ketch1 caused morphological defects, reminiscent of mutants in the miRNA pathway.
statements.note: The abstract reports embryonic lethality for the null allele and miRNA-pathway-like morphological defects for the knockdown.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Besides HYL1, KETCH1 also imports other microprocessor components, such as DICER-LIKE 1, into the nucleus.
statements.evidence: We propose that KETCH1 transports HYL1 from the cytoplasm to the nucleus to constitute functional microprocessor in Arabidopsis
statements.note: Only HYL1 is examined as KETCH1 cargo; the abstract says nothing about nuclear import of any other microprocessor component.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In ketch1 knockdown mutants, the nuclear fraction of HYL1 protein was significantly reduced, and nuclear processing of pri-miRNAs was impaired accordingly.
statements.evidence: Rather, the mutation significantly reduced nuclear portion of HYL1 protein and correspondingly compromised the pri-miRNA processing in the nucleus.
statements.note: The abstract states that the mutation lowered the nuclear portion of HYL1 and compromised nuclear pri-miRNA processing.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knocking down ketch1 lowered miRNA accumulation substantially but left the nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling of miRNAs unchanged.
statements.evidence: ketch1 knockdown mutation also substantially reduced miRNA accumulation, but did not alter nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling of miRNAs.
statements.note: The abstract reports less miRNA accumulation in the knockdown with no change in miRNA shuttling between nucleus and cytoplasm.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Both susi-1 mutant worms and worms kept at low temperature accumulated 26S rRNA carrying oligouridylated 3' tails.
statements.evidence: In susi-1 mutant and in low temperature-treated animals, 3'-tail oligouridylated 26S rRNA accumulated.
statements.note: The abstract reports accumulation of 3'-tail oligouridylated 26S rRNA in both susi-1 mutants and cold-treated animals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Production of risiRNAs, which are complementary in sequence to the 18S and 26S rRNAs, depends on RNA-dependent RNA polymerases.
statements.evidence: risiRNAs show sequence complementary to 18S and 26S rRNAs and require RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRPs) for their production.
statements.note: The abstract states that risiRNAs are complementary to 18S and 26S rRNAs and need RdRPs to be made.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Loss of DIS3L2 in human cells likewise causes oligouridylated rRNA to accumulate.
statements.evidence: SUSI-1 is a homolog of the human DIS3L2 exonuclease involved in 3'-5' degradation of oligouridylated RNAs.
statements.note: Human DIS3L2 is mentioned only as the homolog of SUSI-1; all rRNA experiments were done in C. elegans, so human cells were not tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Stress stimuli such as low temperature and UV irradiation increased risiRNA levels in C. elegans.
statements.evidence: Stress stimuli, including low temperature and UV irradiation, induced the accumulation of risiRNAs.
statements.note: The abstract reports that cold and UV irradiation induced risiRNA accumulation, i.e. raised their levels.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Plants release the miRNAs that signal to neighbouring plants into the soil through their roots.
statements.evidence: This phenomenon has been observed in nematodes and insects, and host Arabidopsis cells secrete exosome-like extracellular vesicles to deliver plant small RNAs into Botrytis cinerea.
statements.note: Vesicle secretion is described only as background for delivery to a fungus; the abstract does not say how or where plants release miRNAs to other plants.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study found that miRNAs made by one plant serve as signals that change gene expression in other plants growing nearby.
statements.evidence: Here we show that micro-RNAs (miRNAs) produced by plants act as signalling molecules affecting gene expression in other, nearby plants.
statements.note: The abstract reports that plant-produced miRNAs act as signalling molecules affecting gene expression in nearby plants.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: RNAi triggered by exogenous miRNAs such as miR156 and miR399 depends on both AGO1 and RDR6.
statements.evidence: Exogenous miRNAs, such as miR156 and miR399, trigger RNAi via a mechanism requiring both AGO1 and RDR6.
statements.note: The abstract states that the RNAi induced by exogenous miR156 and miR399 requires AGO1 and RDR6.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: For exogenous miRNAs to induce RNAi in a receiving plant, secondary small interfering RNAs must be generated.
statements.evidence: This emphasizes that the production of secondary small interfering RNAs is required.
statements.note: The abstract states that production of secondary siRNAs is required for the RNAi triggered by exogenous miRNAs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A large set of ISY1-dependent miRNAs rescued the failure of miRNA-deficient embryonic stem cells to reach the poised state and move on to the primed state.
statements.evidence: We identify a large subset of ISY1-dependent miRNAs that can rescue the inability of miRNA-deficient ESCs to establish the poised state and transition to the primed state.
statements.note: The abstract reports that ISY1-dependent miRNAs restore the ability of miRNA-deficient ESCs to establish the poised state and transition to primed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The poised phase marked by dynamic ISY1 expression has distinct miRNA and mRNA transcriptomes, and poised cells contribute extensively to mouse chimeras.
statements.evidence: Here, we find that highly dynamic ISY1 expression during the naive-to-primed ESC transition defines a specific phase of "poised" pluripotency characterized by distinct miRNA and mRNA transcriptomes and widespread poised cell contribution to mouse chimeras.
statements.note: The abstract describes the ISY1-defined poised phase as having distinct miRNA and mRNA transcriptomes and widespread contribution to chimeras.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ISY1 promotes the departure of embryonic stem cells from naive pluripotency, and its expression is required and sufficient for entering and keeping the poised state.
statements.evidence: Loss- and gain-of-function experiments reveal that ISY1 promotes exit from the naive state and is necessary and sufficient to induce and maintain poised pluripotency
statements.note: Loss- and gain-of-function experiments showed ISY1 promotes naive-state exit and is necessary and sufficient for poised pluripotency.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: ISY1 controls the poised pluripotent state in the same way in human embryonic stem cells.
statements.evidence: Thus, dynamic ISY1 regulates poised pluripotency through miRNAs to control ESC fate.
statements.note: The work is in mouse ESCs and chimeras; the abstract gives no data on human embryonic stem cells.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Aubergine's control of germline stem cell self-renewal depends on piRNAs guiding it to its target mRNAs.
statements.evidence: which promotes translation of self-renewal and differentiation factors by directly binding to its target mRNAs and interacting with translational initiation factors.
statements.note: The abstract says Aub binds its target mRNAs directly but never states whether piRNAs are needed to guide it in this role.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Both self-renewal of germline stem cells and differentiation of their progeny are promoted by Aubergine in the Drosophila ovary.
statements.evidence: Here we report that Aub promotes GSC self-renewal and GSC progeny differentiation.
statements.note: The abstract reports that Aub promotes GSC self-renewal and the differentiation of GSC progeny.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: RNA-iCLIP on cultured germline stem cells detected Aubergine bound to mRNAs that encode self-renewal and differentiation factors.
statements.evidence: RNA-iCLIP results show that Aub binds the mRNAs encoding self-renewal and differentiation factors in cultured GSCs.
statements.note: The RNA-iCLIP result in the abstract shows Aub binding mRNAs for self-renewal and differentiation factors in cultured GSCs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aubergine sustains germline stem cell self-renewal partly by keeping Chk2 from being activated after DNA damage and partly through translational control of self-renewal factors.
statements.evidence: Aub controls GSC self-renewal by preventing DNA-damage-induced Chk2 activation and by translationally controlling the expression of self-renewal factors.
statements.note: The abstract names both mechanisms: preventing DNA-damage-induced Chk2 activation and translational control of self-renewal factors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Breakdown of HYL1 relieves gene silencing, which lets the plant mount an appropriate response to darkness and shade.
statements.evidence: Degradation of HYL1 leads to the release of gene silencing, triggering a proper response to dark and shade.
statements.note: The abstract states that HYL1 degradation releases gene silencing and triggers a proper response to dark and shade.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: During prolonged darkness, the amount of HYL1 protein decreased, but an inactive, phosphorylated pool of HYL1 stayed stable in the nucleus.
statements.evidence: When plants suffer an unusual extended period of light deprivation, the miRNA biogenesis factor HYPONASTIC LEAVES 1 (HYL1) is degraded but an inactive pool of phosphorylated protein remains stable inside the nucleus.
statements.note: The abstract reports HYL1 degradation under extended light deprivation, with a stable inactive phosphorylated pool kept in the nucleus.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Phytochrome photoreceptors detect the light changes that control HYL1 stability.
statements.evidence: Here we show that plants alter microRNA (miRNA) biogenesis in response to light transition.
statements.note: The abstract describes the response to light transitions but never says which photoreceptor, if any, senses them.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Once light returns, HYL1 is rapidly dephosphorylated, which restarts miRNA biogenesis and shifts development toward maximising light capture.
statements.evidence: Upon light restoration, a quick dephosphorylation of HYL1 leads to the reactivation of miRNA biogenesis and a switch toward a developmental program that maximizes the light uptake.
statements.note: The abstract states that quick HYL1 dephosphorylation after light restoration reactivates miRNA biogenesis and switches development to maximise light uptake.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The seed sequence of mir-35 is required, and largely sufficient, for the selective decay of this miRNA family at the embryo-to-larva transition.
statements.evidence: The seed sequence of the miRNA is necessary and largely sufficient for this regulation.
statements.note: The abstract states that the seed sequence is necessary and largely sufficient for the developmentally timed decay of mir-35.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Preventing mir-35 decay at the larval transition causes developmental defects in C. elegans larvae.
statements.evidence: Our findings demonstrate that seed-sequence-specific decay can selectively and coherently regulate all redundant members of a miRNA seed family
statements.note: The abstract describes how the decay works but reports no experiment on what happens to larvae when the decay is blocked.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Enzymatic modifications at the mir-35 3' end were not widespread and did not track with changes in decay.
statements.evidence: Enzymatic modifications of the miRNA 3' end are neither prevalent nor correlated with changes in decay
statements.note: The abstract reports that 3'-end modifications are neither prevalent nor correlated with decay changes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In C. elegans, the abundance of the mir-35 miRNA family decreases selectively as development passes from the embryonic to the larval stage.
statements.evidence: Here, we show that the mir-35 miRNA family undergoes selective decay at the transition from embryonic to larval development in C. elegans.
statements.note: The abstract reports selective decay of the mir-35 family at the embryo-to-larva transition, which lowers its abundance.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Small RNA-driven epimutations arose at a rate roughly 25 times higher than DNA sequence changes and usually had half-lives of only two to three generations.
statements.evidence: We show that epimutations arise spontaneously at a rate approximately 25 times greater than DNA sequence changes and typically have short half-lives of two to three generations.
statements.note: The abstract gives an epimutation rate about 25 times that of DNA sequence changes and typical half-lives of two to three generations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Some small RNA-driven epimutations in C. elegans were still present after ten generations.
statements.evidence: Nevertheless, some epimutations last at least ten generations.
statements.note: The abstract states that some epimutations persist for at least ten generations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study concluded that, without selection, small RNA-mediated epimutations are unlikely to produce long-term divergence.
statements.evidence: Epimutations mediated by small RNAs may thus contribute to evolutionary processes over a short timescale but are unlikely to bring about long-term divergence in the absence of selection.
statements.note: The abstract's conclusion is that small RNA epimutations are unlikely to cause long-term divergence in the absence of selection.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Small RNA-driven epimutations in C. elegans arise preferentially in genes involved in stress responses.
statements.evidence: We use experimental evolution to characterize the rate, spectrum and stability of epimutations driven by small silencing RNAs in the model nematode Caenorhabditis elegans.
statements.note: The abstract says the spectrum of epimutations was characterized but reports nothing about which kinds of genes they affect.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Tethering Armi to a transcript also directs it into primary piRNA processing in Drosophila testes.
statements.evidence: Here we demonstrate that artificial tethering of the piRNA biogenesis factor, Armi, to a transcript is sufficient to direct it into primary processing in Drosophila ovaries and in an ovarian cell culture model.
statements.note: Tethering was tested only in ovaries and an ovarian cell line; the abstract says nothing about testes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the ovarian germline, tethering-induced primary piRNA biogenesis loaded piRNAs into all three PIWI proteins found there.
statements.evidence: Tethering-mediated primary piRNA biogenesis is also functional in the fly ovarian germline and loads all the three PIWI proteins present in this environment.
statements.note: The abstract reports that tethering-driven biogenesis works in the ovarian germline and loads all three PIWI proteins present.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Uridines are favoured at piRNA 5' ends, but transcripts lacking them were still processed, though at lower efficiency.
statements.evidence: Although uridines are preferred for generation of piRNA 5' ends, processing takes place even in their absence, albeit at a lower efficiency.
statements.note: The abstract states that processing occurs without uridines but at a lower efficiency.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In ovarian somatic follicle cells, tethered transcripts were cleaved stepwise in the 5'→3' direction, releasing roughly 24-nt piRNAs with a 5' uridine that load into Piwi.
statements.evidence: In the fly ovarian somatic follicle cells, the transcript becomes cleaved in a stepwise manner, with a 5'→3' directionality, liberating U1-containing ~24 nt piRNAs that are loaded into Piwi.
statements.note: The abstract describes stepwise 5'→3' cleavage yielding U1-containing ~24 nt piRNAs loaded into Piwi.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: TDRKH is needed to generate the whole MIWI-bound piRNA population and makes trimming of MILI-bound piRNAs possible.
statements.evidence: It is required for the production of the entire MIWI-bound piRNA population and enables trimming of MILI-bound piRNAs.
statements.note: The abstract states that TDRKH is required for all MIWI-bound piRNAs and enables trimming of MILI-bound piRNAs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mutations in human TDRKH cause male infertility.
statements.evidence: Our findings identify a mitochondrial surface-based scaffolding mechanism separating the entry and actions of two critical PIWI proteins in the same piRNA pathway to drive piRNA biogenesis and germ cell development.
statements.note: All findings come from mice; the abstract reports nothing about human TDRKH or fertility in men.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: TDRKH selectively brings MIWI, and not MILI, into the piRNA pathway.
statements.evidence: TDRKH specifically recruits MIWI, but not MILI, to engage the piRNA pathway.
statements.note: The abstract states that TDRKH specifically recruits MIWI but not MILI.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: When TDRKH is absent, MIWI fails to reach the intermitochondrial cement, causing a loss of MIWI in the chromatoid body and arrest of spermiogenesis.
statements.evidence: The failure to recruit MIWI to the IMC with TDRKH deficiency results in loss of MIWI in the chromatoid body, leading to spermiogenic arrest and piRNA-independent retrotransposon LINE1 de-repression in round spermatids.
statements.note: The abstract reports that without TDRKH, MIWI is not recruited to the IMC, is lost from the chromatoid body, and spermiogenesis arrests.
